title.narrative: Plateau State Emergency Response for Vulnerable Populations (START)

description.narrative: Bokkos LGA of Plateau state recorded an outbreak of violent attacks between April 2 and 6, 2025 when unknown gunmen invaded six (6) communities and killed at least fifty two (52) people and displaced nearly Two Thousand (2,000) others over several days of attacks in Hurti, Josho, Daffo, and other communities of the locality in Plateau state (which has a history of violence between sedentary farmers and nomadic pastoralists ). Plateau state is one of several ethnically and religiously diverse hinterland states known as Nigeria's Middle Belt, where inter-communal conflict has claimed hundreds of lives in recent years. The violence is often painted as ethno-religious conflict between Muslim herders and mainly Christian farmers. But climate change and the reduction of grazing land through agricultural expansion are also major factors. The reason for the attacks in the six (6) communities/villages in Bokkos-Plateau state is unknown but it has been the worst outbreak of violence since December 2023, when more than 100 people were killed in the same Local Government Area. An estimated 6,000 IDPs are hosted by communities in Bokkos town and Barkin Ladi, LGA and Kwall District of Bassa LGA. The Village Head of Hurti, Mr Maren Aradong, said this when the Secretary to the State Government, Mr Samuel Jatau, led other government officials on an assessment visit to the community on Sunday in Jos. Aradong said that the gunmen also looted foodstuff and other items. They also burnt 383 houses, destroyed foodstuffs, and looted other items. five (5) persons are reported missing in Hurti, two (2) critically injured individuals (including a pregnant woman) are receiving treatment at Plateau Specialist Hospital in Jos, while over Twenty (20) others are admitted at Cottage Hospital, Bokkos Town. this project will provde WASH, NFI, Protection and multipurpose cash transfer services to the selected beneficiaries.
